extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, news industry analysts, and policymakers interested in audience and digital revenue metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines, definitions, and measurement standards used by Pew Research Center to quantify television and digital news audiences, platform presence, mobile optimization, and digital advertising/revenue trends. Includes sample selection rules and methodological caveats used in the report's analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average viewership (network/program level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewership corresponds to the average of quarter‑hour audience for each network or program (e.g., combined average audience for Sunday political talk shows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew reports average quarter‑hour audience and year‑to‑year percent changes. Example: combined average audience for the three networks in 2015 was 9.3 million, up 8% from the year before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted annual averages (Nielsen)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2015, Nielsen provided Pew with weighted annual averages for each network starting with 2008 data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted averages better account for slight differences in the number of programming hours in each broadcast month (used for multi‑year trend comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarter‑hour audience metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewership measurement is based on the average of quarter‑hour audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the basic unit of TV audience measurement in the report; stated explicitly in multiple program-level analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year‑over‑year percent change in audience or revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent change from one year to the next (e.g., 'up 8% from the year before', 'dropped 5% from 2014').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to summarize growth or decline trends across programs, sectors, or revenue categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kantar Media advertising revenue estimates (TV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated advertising revenue for network programs (example: combined revenues for evening broadcast news programs were estimated by Kantar Media for the first three quarters of each year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: reported figures may include only specific telecasts (e.g., Monday–Friday) and specific periods (e.g., Jan 1–Sept 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total digital population (unduplicated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as the unduplicated combination of the desktop (web browsing and video) and mobile traffic figures (websites and associated apps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the baseline for comparing overall digital reach; care required to avoid double counting device/platform overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: comScore metrics and comparison period
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of comScore Media Metrix (Multi‑Platform and Desktop only) to measure unique visitors and minutes per visit, comparing Oct.–Dec. 2014 to Oct.–Dec. 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew analysts worked with comScore to identify and remove entities whose traffic shifts were measurement artifacts rather than organic audience changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance threshold for mobile vs desktop traffic (mobile‑majority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pew considered the difference between a site’s desktop and mobile traffic to be significant if one was at least 10% greater than the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'mobile‑majority' status (e.g., mobile‑majority if mobile visits > desktop visits by >=10%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital‑native publisher sample selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital‑native sites were selected if they were 'born on the web', covered a range of news subjects, had comScore data for the relevant quarters, and received at least 10 million monthly unique visitors (Oct.–Dec. 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis excluded sites without trendable comScore data; resulted in a 40‑site sample for cross‑site analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large gain/loss threshold for site traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: A large loss or gain in average monthly unique visitors or minutes per visit represents at least a 10% difference between 2014 and 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to classify sites as having experienced substantial increases or decreases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile optimization testing method
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile optimization was assessed using the Google PageSpeed Mobile Ready Test across 10 pages per site (selected from RSS feeds or homepage when RSS unavailable), averaging the scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One site produced a tool error and was omitted from the mobile optimization analysis (39 of 40 sites analyzed). This documents the specific test and sampling procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile app availability audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit of Apple App Store, Google Play store, and publishers' websites to determine whether a site had an iOS app, Android app, both, or none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts reported (e.g., number of sites iOS‑only, Android‑only, both, none) to indicate mobile distribution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence on social platforms metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit presence across platforms (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, YouTube, Snapchat) and other extensions (newsletters, podcasts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports counts of how many of the sampled sites were present on each platform (e.g., all 40 on Facebook/Twitter/YouTube; 36 on Instagram; 20–40 counts shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletter and podcast adoption metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and intensity measures for newsletters (how many sites offer newsletters; number of distinct newsletters) and podcasts (how many sites produce podcasts; number of podcasts produced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 35 of 40 sites had email newsletters; 14 sites had multiple newsletters; 19 sites produced podcasts (13 producing more than one; two producing 50 each).

rubrics_metrics.name: Device differences in time‑on‑site (minutes per visit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of minutes per visit between desktop and mobile visitors for each site (e.g., desktop visitors spent more time on 23 of 40 sites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to highlight that while mobile drives visits, desktop often yields longer engagement per visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital advertising spending categories and breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdowns of digital ad spending by platform (mobile vs desktop), by category (display vs search), and by display format (banner, video, rich media, sponsorship/native).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: mobile accounted for 53% of digital ad spending in 2015; display ad spending grew 27% to $26.8B; video ads increased 46% to $7.7B; banner ads accounted for 44% of display spending and grew 13%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of tablets in mobile ad spending
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile ad spending figures include ad spending on tablets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit methodological note clarifying device categorization for mobile totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market concentration metrics for digital ad revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of total digital advertising revenue held by top companies (e.g., Google, Facebook, Yahoo, Microsoft, Twitter accounted for 65% of total digital advertising revenue in 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also reported shares within display and mobile display segments (e.g., Facebook took 30% of total display ad revenue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of digital publisher financial health
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of reported revenue estimates, venture funding rounds, profitability reports, and structural/staffing changes as indicators of publisher financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (Vox Media funding, BuzzFeed revenue and funding, Business Insider investment, Huffington Post revenues) and caveats about limited availability of comprehensive revenue data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local digital publisher survey metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey measures for local digital publishers including percent reporting revenue increases, percent profitable, revenue ranges (e.g., two‑thirds generated $100,000 or less), revenue source composition (local advertising share), and organizational form (percent for‑profit vs nonprofit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example survey: 94 local digital publishers; 70% reported revenue increases in 2014 vs prior year; 47% reported turning a profit; 72% reported local advertising made up half or more of revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit digital news revenue composition metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures for nonprofit digital outlets including median revenue, share of revenue from foundations, earned income, and individual donations/membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Knight Foundation analysis of 20 outlets found median revenue rose to around $518,000 in 2013; foundation funding accounted for 58% of total revenue in 2013; about 23% came from earned income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological caveats and data limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated statements that comprehensive data are not available for the news industry overall; analyses rely on combinations of audience analytics, survey data, audits, and selective vendor data (Nielsen, comScore, Kantar, eMarketer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew documents sampling choices, exclusions for non‑trendable data, and adjustments to remove measurement artifacts. Users should interpret sector‑level findings with these limitations in mind.
